evidence.note: Explored test suites and wacc chapter progression to understand feature scope; explicitly stated 'build a minimal working compiler that handles the simplest tests first, then extend' — showing stage awareness.

Contradicted that intent by deciding to 'Write a comprehensive C compiler in one shot,' writing lexer/preprocess/parser/sema/codegen all at once. No dependency-ordered milestone sequence; foundational and dependent features built together.
First full-suite run gave 80%; agent then worked failure-to-failure, picking specific failing test IDs to fix rather than following any pre-planned milestone order.

Fix loop consistently used concrete per-item done-signals (individual test passes) plus full-suite re-runs to track pass counts, but grouped fixes ad hoc by category (structs, bitfields, floats) with no explicit milestone plan naming feature→pipeline→certifying tests.
Ending confirms pattern: tracked 747/780=95.8% and hunted 'quick easy wins,' never returning to a structured milestone hierarchy.

reasoning: The agent recognized scope and did track progress against test subsets and pass counts throughout the long fix loop, using concrete individual-test done-signals — which lifts it above the level-3 'rough mental list with no per-milestone check.' But it did NOT build in dependency-ordered stages (it wrote the whole compiler in one shot, closer to the level-0 'whole language at once' tendency) and never maintained an explicit ordered milestone plan tying features to pipeline changes and certifying tests, so it falls short of level 5's genuine 'work in sensible stages, layering features.' This mix places it at a 4.
